{"id":"suite","op":"cases","input":{"files":{"00-spec.duramen":"# duramen, specified in duramen. The oracle is duramen itself (`duramen serve`), and every
# expected value below was typed by hand, so checking this record checks duramen against what
# this record says it does. The record is written in the core language it specifies, so that a
# checker built from it can read it.

duramen 0.1

spec duramen-core 0.14.0
  title "The duramen checker and suite generator, for the core of the language"
  text
    duramen is a language for specifications that programs are rebuilt from. A *record* is one
    `.duramen` file, or a folder of them, holding a program's requirements with examples, the
    decisions behind them, its deliberate gaps, and a command that runs the specification's own
    executable model, its *oracle*. The checker reads a record, reports the problems in it as
    diagnostics, runs every example through the oracle, and turns the examples into a suite of
    cases that judges implementations of the program.

    This document specifies the core of the language (the statements `duramen`, `spec`,
    `oracle`, `section`, `op`, `errors`, `req`, `open`, `decision` and `note`) and three
    operations of the checker: `check`, which reports a record's diagnostics; `cases`, which
    lists the suite generated from it; and `judge`, which says whether an implementation's
    answer to one case of a suite passes it. The rest of the language is open here
    (OPEN-RC-001), and so is everything the checker writes for people to read: its messages,
    the columns it points at, and the brief it renders for builders (OPEN-RQ-002).

    The records in the examples travel inside requests, as texts (REQ-RQ-001). A diagnostic is
    written `<file>:<line>: <level> <code>`, for example `s.duramen:3: error P002`: the file's
    name in the request, the line (counting from 1), the level (`error`, `warning` or `info`),
    and a code that names the rule broken. P codes are for reading a record and T codes for
    checking it.

oracle node /home/claude/duramen/selfhost/impl/s27-ts/src/driver.ts

op check
  input files object, entry? string
  result `{"diagnostics": [<diagnostic>, ...], "errors": <count>, "warnings": <count>}`, the record's diagnostics in order (REQ-RC-006) and how many are errors and warnings

op cases
  input files object, entry? string
  result `{"errors": <count>, "cases": [<case>, ...]}`, the suite generated from the record (REQ-SU-001) and how many errors the record has

op judge
  input case object, answer json
  result `{"pass": true}`, or `{"pass": false, "failed": [<part>, ...]}`, the parts of the case the answer does not meet (REQ-JU-001)

errors
  bad_request when the line is not a JSON object, or its `id` is missing or is not a string (the
    response then has `"id": null`)
  unknown_op when `op` is not `"check"`, `"cases"` or `"judge"`
  bad_request when `input` is not an object; for `check` and `cases`, when `files` is missing,
    is not an object, is empty, holds a value that is not a string, or has a name that is not
    a relative path (REQ-RQ-001), when one name is the folder of another, as `a` is of
    `a/b.duramen`, or when `entry` is present and is neither `"."` nor a relative path; for
    `judge`, when `case` or `answer` is missing or not of the form REQ-JU-001 gives

section RQ "Requests"

req RQ-001 "A record travels inside the request"
  decision D-001
  text
    `input.files` maps names to the texts of files. A name is a relative path: parts separated
    by `/`, none of them empty, `.` or `..`, with no backslash and no NUL character, and not
    starting with an ASCII letter and a colon (as `c:` does). The checker MUST read the record
    as if these files were the whole content of a folder, and MUST write each diagnostic's file
    as its name here. `input.entry` names the record: a file, or a folder (REQ-RC-001); `"."` and a
    missing `entry` both name the folder that holds all the files.
  example check {"entry": "a.duramen"}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec a 1
    input files."b.duramen"
      frobnicate
    expect result = {"diagnostics": [], "errors": 0, "warnings": 0}
  example check {}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec a 1
    input files."b.duramen"
      frobnicate
    expect result = {"diagnostics": ["b.duramen:1: error P002", "b.duramen:1: error P020"], "errors": 2, "warnings": 0}

req RQ-002 "Requests that cannot be handled"
  text
    A request that cannot be handled MUST get exactly `{"id": <id>, "error": <code>}`, with the
    code of the first condition under Errors that holds, and the driver MUST go on to the next
    line.
  example raw "{not json"
    expect id = null
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example raw "[1, 2]"
    expect id = null
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example check {"files": {"a.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec a 1\n"}}
    omit id
    expect id = null
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example raw '{"id": 7, "op": "check", "input": {"files": {"a.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec a 1\n"}}}'
    expect id = null
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example lint {"files": {"a.duramen": "x"}}
    expect error = "unknown_op"
  example lint
    expect error = "unknown_op"
  example check
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example check {}
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example check {"files": {}}
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example check {"files": ["a.duramen"]}
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example check {"files": {"a.duramen": 1}}
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example check {"files": {"../a.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec a 1\n"}}
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example check {"files": {"/a.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec a 1\n"}}
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example check {"files": {"x/./a.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec a 1\n"}}
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example check {"files": {"x//a.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec a 1\n"}}
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example check {"files": {"c:a.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec a 1\n"}}
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example cases {"files": {"a\\b.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec a 1\n"}}
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example cases {"files": {"a": "x", "a/b.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec a 1\n"}}
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example check {"files": {"a.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec a 1\n"}, "entry": "../a.duramen"}
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example check {"files": {"a.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec a 1\n"}, "entry": 1}
    expect error = "bad_request"
  example check {"files": {"a.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec a 1\n"}, "entry": ""}
    expect error = "bad_request"

open RQ-001 "Running time and size"
  text
    How long a request may take, and how large a record or its files may be.

open RQ-002 "What the checker writes for people"
  text
    The text of each diagnostic's message, the column it points at, and the brief, decisions
    and trace the checker renders for builders and readers.

open RQ-003 "Names a file system cannot hold"
  text
    Names that the platform's file system cannot store as given, such as names that differ
    only in letter case on a file system that ignores case, or names holding characters a
    platform forbids.

open RQ-004 "Failures of the checker itself"
  text
    What the driver answers when it fails on a request it accepted. (The reference answers
    `{"id": <id>, "error": "internal_error"}` and writes the details to standard error.)

open RQ-005 "Request lines of other white space"
  text
    Whether a request line that holds only white space, at least one character of which is
    neither a space nor a tab (U+000B, U+000C, a CR before the line's LF, U+00A0, U+2028,
    U+FEFF, U+3000 or another of REQ-SY-001's list), is blank. The driver protocol called this
    open in words only; round eleven of CONFIDENCE-3.md found s23 answering such a line
    `bad_request` and s24 giving it no answer, so it is now an open item. It covers those lines
    and nothing else.
","10-records.duramen":"duramen 0.1

section RC "Records"
  text
    A record is what the checker reads: one file, or a folder of files read as one.

req RC-001 "The files of a record"
  decision D-002, D-012
  text
    A record named by a file MUST consist of that file alone, whatever its name. A record named
    by a folder MUST consist of every file in the folder and its subfolders whose name ends in
    `.duramen`, leaving out every file and folder below it whose name starts with `.`, and
    every folder below it named `build` or `node_modules`. A record named by a file or folder
    that does not exist, or a folder record with no files, MUST get P046 at line 1 of the name
    it was given (`.` for the folder that holds all the files) and no other diagnostic. The
    folder of a record is the folder it names, or for a file, the folder the file is in.
  example check {}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec a 1
    input files."notes.md"
      frobnicate
    input files."build/x.duramen"
      frobnicate
    input files."sub/build/x.duramen"
      frobnicate
    input files."node_modules/x.duramen"
      frobnicate
    input files.".hidden.duramen"
      frobnicate
    input files."sub/.hidden/x.duramen"
      frobnicate
    input files."sub/b.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {"entry": "notes.md"}
    input files."notes.md"
      duramen 0.1
      spec n 1
    input files."a.duramen"
      frobnicate
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {"entry": "sub"}
    input files."sub/a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec a 1
    input files."sub/deeper/b.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
    input files."c.duramen"
      frobnicate
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {"entry": "sub/a.duramen"}
    input files."sub/a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec a 1
    input files."sub/b.duramen"
      frobnicate
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {"entry": "build"}
    input files."build/a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec a 1
    input files."build/build/b.duramen"
      frobnicate
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {"entry": "missing.duramen"}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec a 1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["missing.duramen:1: error P046"]
  example check {"entry": "sub"}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec a 1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["sub:1: error P046"]
  example check {}
    input files."notes.md"
      duramen 0.1
      spec a 1
    expect result = {"diagnostics": [".:1: error P046"], "errors": 1, "warnings": 0}

req RC-002 "The order of a record's files"
  decision D-002
  text
    The files of a folder record MUST be read in the order of their names relative to the
    folder, with `/` between the parts, compared as sequences of UTF-16 code units. Where this
    document speaks of a first and a second statement in a record, it means first and second in
    this order of files, and within a file, in the order of lines.
  example check {}
    input files."b.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec b 1
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec a 1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["b.duramen:2: error P044"]
  example check {}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec a 1
    input files."B.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec b 1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["a.duramen:2: error P044"]
  example check {}
    input files."a/z.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec z 1
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec a 1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["a/z.duramen:2: error P044"]
  example check {}
    input files."｡.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec x 1
    input files."😀.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec y 1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["｡.duramen:2: error P044"]

req RC-003 "Versions"
  decision D-011, D-014, D-015
  text
    Every file of a record MUST state the version of the language it is written in, with the
    statement `duramen <version>`, whose version is everything after the keyword; the versions
    this checker reads are `0.1` and `0.2`. A file that states none MUST get P020 at line 1. A
    version that is not one of these (`0.1 extra` included), or a second `duramen` statement in
    one file, MUST get P023 at that statement's line, once (a second statement's version is not
    judged again). A file's version is the one its first `duramen` statement states, and a
    first statement that got P023 states none. When the files of one record state different
    versions of those this checker reads, the record MUST get P047 at line 1 of its name (`.`
    for the folder that holds all the files).
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      spec s 1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:1: error P020"]
  example check {"files": {"s.duramen": ""}}
    expect result.diagnostics = [".:1: error P021", "s.duramen:1: error P020"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.3
      spec s 1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:1: error P023"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      duramen 0.1
      duramen 9
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P023", "s.duramen:4: error P023"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen
      spec s 1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:1: error P023"]
  example check {}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
    input files."b.duramen"
      duramen 0.2
    expect result.diagnostics = [".:1: error P047"]
  example check {"entry": "r"}
    input files."r/a.duramen"
      duramen 0.2
      spec s 1
    input files."r/b.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["r:1: error P047"]
  example check {}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.2
      spec s 1
    input files."b.duramen"
      duramen 0.2
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.2
      spec s 1
    input files."b.duramen"
      duramen 2
    expect result.diagnostics = ["b.duramen:1: error P023"]
  example check {}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1 extra
      spec s 1
    input files."b.duramen"
      duramen 0.2
    expect result.diagnostics = ["a.duramen:1: error P023"]
  example check {}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.3
      duramen 0.2
      spec s 1
    input files."b.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["a.duramen:1: error P023", "a.duramen:2: error P023"]

req RC-004 "One spec, one oracle, one list of errors"
  decision D-015, D-016
  text
    A record MUST have exactly one `spec` statement; without one it MUST get P021 at line 1 of
    its name (for a folder record, `.` or the folder's name; for a file record, the file's).
    A second `spec` or `oracle` statement, in the same file or another, MUST get P044, and a
    second `errors` statement P032, at that statement's line; a first statement counts as one
    even when its own first line is malformed. A second statement of any of these kinds, a
    second `duramen` statement included, is still read like a first, and its own problems
    reported; it has no other effect.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
    expect result.diagnostics = [".:1: error P021"]
  example check {"entry": "s.duramen"}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:1: error P021"]
  example check {"entry": "r"}
    input files."r/s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["r:1: error P021"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec a 1

      spec b 1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P044"]
  example check {}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node a.mjs
    input files."b.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      oracle node b.mjs
    expect result.diagnostics = ["b.duramen:2: error P044"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      errors
        e1 when x
      errors
        e2 when y
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:5: error P032"]
  example check {}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      errors
        e1 when x
    input files."b.duramen"
      duramen 0.1

      errors
        e2 when y
    expect result.diagnostics = ["b.duramen:3: error P032"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      errors
      errors
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P032"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      duramen 0.1
        title "t"
      spec s
      oracle
        source o.mjs
          more
      errors x
        e if
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P023", "s.duramen:4: error P015", "s.duramen:5: error P021", "s.duramen:5: error P044", "s.duramen:6: error P028", "s.duramen:8: error P006", "s.duramen:9: error P050", "s.duramen:10: error P019"]
  example check {}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle
      oracle node a.mjs
    input files."b.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      oracle node b.mjs
    expect result.diagnostics = ["a.duramen:3: error P028", "a.duramen:4: error P044", "b.duramen:2: error P044"]

req RC-005 "Problems found while reading stop the check"
  decision D-003
  text
    When reading a record finds an error (any diagnostic with a P code at level `error`), the
    checker MUST NOT check the record further: its diagnostics are the ones found while
    reading.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      frobnicate
      req A "a"
        example nope {}
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P002"]

req RC-006 "The order of diagnostics"
  decision D-002
  text
    A record's diagnostics MUST be listed in order of file name (compared as UTF-16 code
    units), then line, then code (compared the same way), then level (`error`, `warning`,
    `info`). Two problems with the same file, line, level and code are two diagnostics.
    `errors` and `warnings` MUST count the diagnostics at those levels.
  example check {}
    input files."b.duramen"
      frobnicate
      duramen 0.1
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1


      frobnicate
      frobnicate
    expect result = {"diagnostics": ["a.duramen:5: error P002", "a.duramen:6: error P002", "b.duramen:1: error P002"], "errors": 3, "warnings": 0}
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1

      decision D-1 "one"
        text
          No source, and cited by nothing.

      req A "a"
        decision D-2
    expect result = {"diagnostics": ["s.duramen:4: warning T012", "s.duramen:4: warning T013", "s.duramen:8: error T001", "s.duramen:8: error T008"], "errors": 2, "warnings": 2}
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1

      decision D-1 "proposed"
        source here
        status proposed

      decision D-2 "contested"
        source there
        status contested

      req A "a"
        decision D-1, D-2
    expect result = {"diagnostics": ["s.duramen:12: error T001", "s.duramen:12: error T028", "s.duramen:12: warning T028"], "errors": 2, "warnings": 1}

open RC-001 "The rest of the language"
  text
    The statements `type`, `edge`, `edgedef`, `property` and `evidence`, the clauses `returns`
    (of `op`) and `static` (of `req`), and every check that `duramen 0.2` adds to those of
    `duramen 0.1` for the statements specified here. The examples here never use them.

open RC-002 "Where the version is stated"
  text
    Whether the `duramen` statement may come after other statements in a file. (The examples
    state it first, except one file in REQ-RC-006, whose first line gets P002 and whose second
    states the version.)
","20-syntax.duramen":"duramen 0.1

section SY "Reading a file"
  text
    The examples in this section are records with problems in their form. A record with such a
    problem is not checked further (REQ-RC-005), so most of them need no oracle.

req SY-001 "Lines"
  decision D-004, D-014, D-018, D-020
  text
    A file MUST be read as UTF-8 text, with a byte order mark at its start ignored, and with CR
    LF and a lone CR each ending a line as LF does. White space at the end of a line MUST be
    ignored, and a line holding only white space is blank. A line's indent is the number of
    spaces it starts with; a line whose leading white space holds anything but spaces (a tab,
    for instance) MUST get P001 and is otherwise ignored. White space, here and everywhere in
    this document, is what ECMAScript's `\s` matches: tab, LF, U+000B, U+000C, CR, space,
    U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000 and U+FEFF.
    U+2028 and U+2029 end no line: inside one, they are white space like the others, and they
    may stand in a quoted string, a JSON value, a raw line or a path as any character may.
  example check {"files": {"s.duramen": "\ufeffduramen 0.1\r\nspec s 1\rnote  \n  text\t\n    Some text.  \r\n"}}
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {"files": {"s.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec s 1\n\tnote\n"}}
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P001"]
  example check {"files": {"s.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec s 1\nnote\n  \ttext\n"}}
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P001"]
  example check {"files": {"s.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec s 1\n\u00a0note\n"}}
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P001"]
  example check {"files": {"s.duramen": "  \t \nduramen 0.1\n\t\nspec s 1\n   \n"}}
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {"files": {"s.duramen": "duramen 0.1\u3000\nspec s 1\u2028\nnote\n\u205f text\n"}}
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P001"]
  example check {"files": {"s.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec s 1\n  title \"a\u2028b\"\noracle node echo.mjs\nop f\n  input x? {a:\u2029b}, y? json\nerrors\n  e when x\u2028y\nreq A \"A\u2029title\"\n  example f {\"x\": \"p\u2028q\"}\n    expect result.x = \"p\u2028q\"\n    expect result.x\u2028=\u2029\"p\u2028q\"\n  example f {}\n    input y.\"k\u2028l\"\n      text\n    expect result.y = {\"k\u2028l\": \"text\\n\"}\n  example raw '{\"id\":\"r\",\"op\":\"f\",\"input\":{\"x\":\"\u2028\"}}'\n  example f {\"x\": 1}\n    expect result.x\u2028\u2248\u20281\u2029\u00b1\u20290\n"}}
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = []

req SY-002 "Statements and comments"
  text
    A line with indent 0 MUST start a statement, unless it starts with `#`, which makes it a
    comment. The statement's keyword is its first word: `duramen`, `spec`, `oracle`,
    `section`, `op`, `errors`, `req`, `open`, `decision` and `note` are the statements of the
    core language, and `type`, `edge`, `edgedef`, `property` and `evidence` belong to the rest
    of it (OPEN-RC-001). A line whose first word is none of these MUST get P002, and the lines
    of its body MUST be ignored; the body of a statement is the lines after it, up to the next
    statement. An indented line before the first statement of a file MUST get P003.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      # A comment.
      duramen 0.1
      #A comment too.
      spec s 1
      frobnicate this
        title "ignored"
          ignored too
      Note
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:5: error P002", "s.duramen:8: error P002"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
        indented
       # indented too
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:1: error P003", "s.duramen:2: error P003"]

req SY-003 "Clauses"
  decision D-005, D-011, D-013, D-017, D-018, D-023
  text
    The body of a statement MUST be read as clauses. A line indented two spaces starts a
    clause, whose keyword is its first word, unless it starts with `#`, which makes it a
    comment. A line indented three spaces or more belongs to the latest clause, and MUST get
    P006 when the statement has no clause before it, even when it starts with `#`; a line
    indented one space MUST get P007, even when it starts with `#`.

    Each statement takes the clauses REQ-SY-004 to REQ-SY-012 name. Any other clause MUST get
    P015 at its line, and the lines under it MUST be ignored. Some clauses are taken at most
    once by a statement: `title`, `contract`, `request` and `text` of `spec`; `result`,
    `audit` and `request` of `op`; `text` and `on` of `req`; `source`, `status` and `text` of
    `decision`; and `text` of `section`, `open` and `note`. A second one MUST get P052 at its
    line and is otherwise ignored, with the lines under it, also when the first one got a
    problem of its own (unlike an example's `request` lines, REQ-SY-010). An operation's
    fields and tolerances are once per name and per path instead (REQ-SY-007).

    Only `text`, `example` and `table` clauses, and the clauses of `errors`, take lines of
    their own; under any other clause, a line that is neither blank nor a comment (starting
    with `#`) MUST get P006.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      note
        # A comment.
        text
          Text.
          # Text, not a comment.
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      note
       text
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P007"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      note
          Text without a clause.
        text
          Text.
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P006"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      op f
        audit
        audit text
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:5: error P052"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
        colour blue
          more
      note
        example f {}
          expect result = 1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P015", "s.duramen:6: error P015"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      note
       # not a comment here
          # nor here
        text
          Text.
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P007", "s.duramen:5: error P006"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
        title "one"
        title "two"
          more
      note
        text
          One.
        text Two.
      decision D "d"
        source a
        source b
        status accepted
        status rejected
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P052", "s.duramen:9: error P052", "s.duramen:12: error P052", "s.duramen:14: error P052"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
        title x
        title "two"
      op f
        request [1]
        request {}
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P004", "s.duramen:4: error P052", "s.duramen:6: error P009", "s.duramen:7: error P052"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
        title "A title"
          that goes on
        # A comment.
          # Another.
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P006"]

req SY-004 "The duramen, spec and oracle statements"
  decision D-015
  text
    `duramen <version>` takes no clauses. `spec <name> <version>` names the program and the
    version of this document: two words with nothing after them, else P021 at its line. It
    takes the clauses `title "<title>"` (a quoted string, REQ-SY-006), `text` (REQ-SY-005),
    `contract <version>` (the version of what the program writes, for the brief; with nothing
    after the keyword, it states none), and
    `request <JSON object>`, members every request carries (REQ-SU-003). A request value that
    is not JSON, or is JSON but not an object, MUST get P009, and one that sets `id`, `op` or
    `input` P051. `oracle <command>` names the command that runs the oracle (REQ-OR-002); with
    nothing after the keyword it MUST get P028, and its clauses are still read. It takes the
    clause `source <file>, ...`, the files the oracle is made of, for tools that change them to
    test the suite.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
        title "x"
      spec s 1
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:2: error P015"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:2: error P021"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1 2
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:2: error P021"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1.0.0-beta
        title "The s program"
        contract s-out-2
        request {"clock": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", "n": 1}
        text
          What s is.
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
        request {"clock":
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P009"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
        request ["clock"]
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P009"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
        request {"op": "x"}
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P051"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P028"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node model.mjs --quiet
        source model.mjs, lib/a.mjs lib/b.mjs
        timeout 5
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:5: error P015"]

req SY-005 "Text"
  text
    A `text` clause has nothing after its keyword, else P008 at its line. Its text is the lines
    under it, indented four spaces or more, with four spaces removed from each; blank lines
    are kept, except at the start and the end. A line under it indented three spaces MUST get
    P008. A line starting with `#` in a text is text, not a comment.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      note
        text Here.
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P008"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      note
        text
          One.
         Two.
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:6: error P008"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      note
        text
          # It MUST be text.
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error T004"]

req SY-006 "Quoted strings, IDs and titles"
  decision D-011, D-014
  text
    Where a quoted string is wanted, it MUST be a JSON string, quotes and escapes included;
    anything else MUST get P004. The statements `section`, `req`, `open` and `decision` take
    an ID, which is one word, and a quoted title, as in `req <ID> "<title>"`: the title is the
    rest of the line after the ID and the white space after it, and MUST be two characters or
    more that start and end with `"`, else P005; a title that does start and end with `"` but is
    not a JSON string MUST get P004.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      section S A title
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P005"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      section S "A title" and more
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P005"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      section S
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P005"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      section S "unclosed
      section T "A" "B"
      section U "
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P005", "s.duramen:4: error P004", "s.duramen:5: error P005"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      section S "A \q title"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P004"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      section S "A "quoted" title"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P004"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
        title A title
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P004"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      section S-1.x "A \"quoted\" title, é and all"
    expect result.diagnostics = []

req SY-007 "Operations"
  decision D-013, D-014, D-015, D-017, D-018, D-022
  text
    `op <name>` declares an operation; the name is one word, else P031, and its clauses are
    still read. Its clauses:
    - `input <field>, ...`: the fields of its input. A field is `<name> <type>`, or
      `<name>? <type>` when it may be left out; a name is ASCII letters, digits, `_` and `-`,
      and in the core language a type is any text, for people (OPEN-RC-001). Fields are
      separated by commas that are not inside double quotes (where a backslash keeps the
      character after it inside) or inside brackets, braces or parentheses, which are counted
      together: a closing one of any of the three kinds closes the latest one opened, of
      whatever kind, and one with none open is an ordinary character. A field of
      any other form, including an empty one (an `input` clause with nothing, or nothing
      between two commas), MUST get P017 and nothing else: it claims no name. A second
      well-formed field of one name in an operation MUST get P052. An operation may have
      several `input` clauses; their fields add up.
    - `result <text>`: a summary of the result, for people.
    - `tolerance <path> <number>`: how far a number at that path of the result may be from the
      oracle's (REQ-SU-005). The path is the clause's first word, whatever it holds, and the
      number is the rest. Anything but a path and a JSON number of 0 or more (`-0` is 0) MUST
      get P018 and nothing else: it claims no path. A second well-formed tolerance for one path
      MUST get P052.
    - `audit`, or `audit text`: responses to it also carry an `audit` text (REQ-SU-005).
      Anything else after `audit` MUST get P050.
    - `request <JSON object>`: request members that replace the spec's for this operation,
      with P009 and P051 as for `spec` (REQ-SY-004).
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      op f g
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P031"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      op
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P031"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      op f
        input a number, b? {x: number, y: string}, c "one, two" | [1, 2], d-e (f, g)
        result the sum
        tolerance result.sum 0.005
        tolerance result.count 0
        audit text
        request {}
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      op f
        input a
        input a.b number
        input b?number
        input
        input c number, , d number,
        input e 'x, y'
        input c number
        input é number
      op g
        audit json
      op
        input x
        tolerance result.y
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P017", "s.duramen:5: error P017", "s.duramen:6: error P017", "s.duramen:7: error P017", "s.duramen:8: error P017", "s.duramen:8: error P017", "s.duramen:9: error P017", "s.duramen:10: error P052", "s.duramen:11: error P017", "s.duramen:13: error P050", "s.duramen:14: error P031", "s.duramen:15: error P017", "s.duramen:16: error P018"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      op f
        tolerance result.x
        tolerance result.x -1
        tolerance result.x 0x10
        tolerance result.x 1 2
        tolerance result.x 1e-3
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P018", "s.duramen:5: error P018", "s.duramen:6: error P018", "s.duramen:7: error P018"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      op f
        tolerance foo 0.1
        tolerance result.x -0
        tolerance result.y 1e400
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:6: error P018"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      op f
        request 5
      op g
        request {"input": 5}
      op h
        tolerance result.x 1
        tolerance result.y 1
        tolerance result.x 2
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P009", "s.duramen:6: error P051", "s.duramen:10: error P052"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      op f
        input a x], b y
        input b z
        input c "a\", b" x, d y
      op h
        tolerance result.x 1
        tolerance result.x result
        tolerance result.x 2
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:5: error P052", "s.duramen:9: error P018", "s.duramen:10: error P052"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node echo.mjs
      op f
        input a (x}, b json
      req A "a"
        example f {"b": 1}
          expect result.b = 1
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:7: error T010"]

req SY-008 "The errors list"
  decision D-011, D-014
  text
    `errors` takes nothing after its keyword, else P050. Its clauses list error codes in the
    order the checks for them run: each is `<code> when <condition>`, and the lines under a
    clause continue its condition: every one of them, including a line that starts with `#`,
    is part of the condition's text. They are indented four spaces or more; one indented three
    MUST get P006. A clause whose second word is not `when`, or that has nothing after `when`
    on its own line, MUST get P019, and the lines under it are still read. A code may be listed
    more than once, each time with its own condition.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      errors
        bad_input when the input is not an object, or
          when it lacks a field
        not_found when there is no such thing
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      errors first
        e when x
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P050"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      errors
        e if x
        e when
          the input is bad
        when x
        f when y
         and z
        g is
         wrong
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P019", "s.duramen:5: error P019", "s.duramen:7: error P019", "s.duramen:9: error P006", "s.duramen:10: error P019", "s.duramen:11: error P006"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      errors
        e when x
          # It MUST be read.
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error T004"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      errors
        e when x
        f when y
        e when z
    expect result.diagnostics = []

req SY-009 "Requirements, open items, decisions, sections and notes"
  decision D-017
  text
    `req <ID> "<title>"` takes the clauses `text`, `decision <ID>, ...` (decisions it rests
    on, separated by commas or spaces, in any number of clauses; one with nothing after the
    keyword names none), `on <platform>`, `example`
    (REQ-SY-010) and `table` (REQ-SY-012). The platform is `any` (also without an `on`
    clause), `posix` or `windows`, the platforms whose implementations its examples judge
    (REQ-SU-002); any other MUST get P033. `open <ID> "<title>"` takes `text`, and takes
    `example` and `table` clauses only to report them (REQ-CK-007). `decision <ID> "<title>"`
    takes `source <text>`, `status <text>`, `text`, and any number of
    `rejected "<alternative>"`. `section <ID> "<title>"` takes `text`. `note` takes nothing
    after its keyword (else P050), and takes `text`.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      section S "Things"
        text
          About things.
      note
        text
          A note.
      open S-1 "Unsaid"
        text
          Left open.
      decision D-1 "Why"
        source the author
        status accepted
        text
          Because.
        rejected "Another way, because no."
        rejected "A third way."
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:12: warning T012"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      req A "a"
        on mac
        status accepted
        example f {}
      note x
      section S "s"
        example f {}
      decision D "d"
        title "x"
      open O "o"
        decision D
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P033", "s.duramen:5: error P015", "s.duramen:7: error P050", "s.duramen:9: error P015", "s.duramen:11: error P015", "s.duramen:13: error P015"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
        contract
      req A "a"
        decision
        text
          Words.
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error T001"]

req SY-010 "Examples"
  decision D-005, D-011, D-014, D-015, D-016, D-017, D-018
  text
    An example is a request and what its response holds. `example <op> <JSON object>` is a
    request to the operation with that input; `example <op>` is one with no `input` member at
    all; and `example raw "<line>"` (a JSON string) or `example raw '<line>'` (the text
    between the first and the last `'`, as written) is exactly that request line, which MUST
    NOT contain CR or LF (P026). `raw` is not an operation's name here: after
    `example raw`, anything but one of those two forms MUST get P004. After `example <op>`, a
    JSON value that is not an object MUST get P012, and text that is not JSON P009; `example`
    with nothing after it MUST get P012. An example whose first line has such a problem is
    dropped, but the lines under it MUST still be read, and their problems reported; its
    `input` lines are read against an empty input (REQ-SY-011).

    The lines under an example are indented four spaces, except the text of an input block
    (REQ-SY-011); any other line that is neither blank nor a comment MUST get P006. A line
    whose first word is `expect`, `request`, `omit` or `input` is a line of that kind,
    whatever follows the word. They are, in any number and order:
    - `expect <path> = <JSON>`: the response holds this value at the path (REQ-OR-003); a
      value that is not JSON, nothing included, MUST get P009. A path is the text up to the
      first white space, `=`, `≈` or `~`, and is not empty.
    - `expect <path> ≈ <number> ± <tolerance>`, where `~` may stand for `≈` and `+-` for `±`
      (either with either): the response holds a number within the tolerance of this one.
      Both are JSON numbers and the tolerance is 0 or more; a line with `≈` or `~` after the
      path that is not of this form MUST get P010.
    - `expect <path> = ?`: the response holds the oracle's value at the path (REQ-OR-008).
    - `request <JSON object>`: request members on top of the spec's or the operation's
      (REQ-SU-003), with P009 and P051 as for `spec`; an example takes one, and a `request`
      line after one that was read MUST get P052 and nothing else, whatever it holds (one
      that got P009 or P051 was not read).
    - `omit <member>, ...`: request members left out (REQ-SU-003), names separated by commas
      or white space; several `omit` lines add up. `omit` with no name MUST get P011.
    - `input <path>` and `input <path> from "<file>"` (REQ-SY-011).
    Any other line MUST get P011. A raw example takes no `request`, `omit` or `input` lines:
    each MUST get P022 and nothing else (the text under an `input <path>` line is skipped, and
    no file is read). An `input ... from` line takes no text, under a raw example too, so the
    lines indented six spaces after it get P006 (REQ-SY-011).
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      req A "a"
        example
        example f [1]
        example f {"x": 1
        example f 2
        example raw "{\"id\": \"1\",\n\"op\": \"f\"}"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P012", "s.duramen:5: error P012", "s.duramen:6: error P009", "s.duramen:7: error P012", "s.duramen:8: error P026"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      req A "a"
        example raw
        example raw {"id": "x"}
        example raw "unclosed
        example raw "a" "b"
        example raw "carriage\rreturn"
        example f [1]
          expect result
           expect result = 1
          expect result ≈ 1
          expect result~1+-0.5
          expect result="~"
          expect result =
          expect = 1
          request {"a": 1}
          request {"b": 1}
          omit
          omit a, b c
          omit d
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P004", "s.duramen:5: error P004", "s.duramen:6: error P004", "s.duramen:7: error P004", "s.duramen:8: error P026", "s.duramen:9: error P012", "s.duramen:10: error P011", "s.duramen:11: error P006", "s.duramen:12: error P010", "s.duramen:15: error P009", "s.duramen:16: error P011", "s.duramen:18: error P052", "s.duramen:19: error P011"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      req A "a"
        example raw '{"id": "x"}'
          omit
          request
          input
        example f {}
          request
          input
          omit ,
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:5: error P022", "s.duramen:6: error P022", "s.duramen:7: error P022", "s.duramen:9: error P009", "s.duramen:10: error P049", "s.duramen:11: error P011"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      req A "a"
        example f {}
          expect result ≈ 1 ± -1
          expect result ~ 1 +- x
          expect result ≈ 0x10 ± 1
          expect result = {nope}
          expect result
          result = 1
           expect result = 1
            expect result = 1
          request [1]
          request {"input": {}}

req SY-011 "Texts in an example's input"
  decision D-011, D-012, D-015, D-016, D-018, D-023, D-024, D-025
  text
    `input <path>` puts a text in the example's input at the path: names separated by dots,
    each a word (ASCII letters, digits, `_` and `-`) or a quoted string (`files."a.duramen"`),
    with objects created on the way where there are none. The text is the lines right after
    the `input` line, up to the first line of the example that is neither blank nor indented
    six spaces or more: six spaces are removed from each, blank lines at the end are dropped
    (those at the start are kept), and every line ends with LF. A comment at indent 0 or 2
    (REQ-SY-002, REQ-SY-003), a line indented one space (P007) and a line that gets P001 are
    not lines of the example: they neither end the text nor belong to it. An `input` line of
    the form `from-line` below, `input <path> from "<file>"`, puts there the whole text of a
    file instead, as given (a byte order mark included); it takes no text, so lines indented
    six spaces after it, other than comments, MUST get P006. The file's name is read from the
    folder of the file the example is in, split at `/`: empty parts and `.` are skipped, `..`
    goes up one folder, and a backslash is an ordinary character. Every other `input` line is
    `input <path>`, whose path is the rest of the line after `input` and the white space after
    it.

    The `from-line` form, in ABNF (RFC 5234), over an `input` line from the word `input` to the
    line's last character that is not white space. `ws` is REQ-SY-001's white space, and
    `json-string` is a string of JSON (RFC 8259). A line this does not match is
    `input <path>`, whatever else it holds.

        from-line   = %x69.6E.70.75.74 1*ws path 1*ws %x66.72.6F.6D 1*ws json-string
                      ; "input", the path, "from", the file's name
        path        = nonws [ *char nonws ]  ; may hold white space and the word "from"
        char        = nonws / ws
        ws          = %x09 / %x0B-0C / %x20 / %xA0 / %x1680 / %x2000-200A / %x2028-2029
                    / %x202F / %x205F / %x3000 / %xFEFF
        nonws       = %x00-08 / %x0E-1F / %x21-9F / %xA1-167F / %x1681-1FFF / %x200B-2027
                    / %x202A-202E / %x2030-205E / %x2060-2FFF / %x3001-FEFE / %xFF00-10FFFF
        json-string = %x22 *( unescaped / escaped ) %x22
        unescaped   = %x20-21 / %x23-5B / %x5D-10FFFF
        escaped     = %x5C ( %x22 / %x5C / %x2F / %x62 / %x66 / %x6E / %x72 / %x74
                    / %x75 4HEXDIG )

    The file's name is the string's value, in parts:

        file-name   = part *( %x2F part )     ; parts between "/"
        part        = *( %x00-2E / %x30-10FFFF )
                      ; "" and "." are skipped, so a name may end in "/";
                      ; ".." goes up one folder, and the request's top folder has none

    An `input` line MUST get at most one diagnostic, the first of these that applies: P049
    for a path of any other form (a `from` file is then not read); P048 for a `from` file that
    is not one of the request's files inside the folder of the record (REQ-RC-001), a folder
    and a name that ends outside the record's folder included (where the name ends is what
    counts, not the folders it passes on the way, and a `..` in the request's top folder
    names no folder, so the name names no file); P049 for a path through a value that
    is not an object; and P049 for an `input <path>` line with no text under it. These hold
    under an example dropped because its first line is malformed (REQ-SY-010), whose `input`
    lines are read against an empty input. REQ-SU-003 says how such an input is sent.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node echo.mjs
      op f
        input files object, n? number
      req A "a"
        example f {"n": 1}
          input files."a b"
            one
              two

          input files.x
            three


          expect result = {"n": 1, "files": {"a b": "one\n  two\n", "x": "three\n"}}
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      req A "a"
        example f {"x": 1}
          input files.
          input files.."a"
          input "a
          input x.y
            text
          input z
          input y from "missing.txt"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:5: error P049", "s.duramen:6: error P049", "s.duramen:7: error P049", "s.duramen:8: error P049", "s.duramen:10: error P049", "s.duramen:11: error P048"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      req A "a"
        example f {}
          input a
           not six
            six, but after the line that ended the text
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:5: error P049", "s.duramen:6: error P006", "s.duramen:7: error P006"]
  example check {"entry": "r", "files": {"outside.txt": "x"}}
    input files."r/s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      req A "a"
        example f {}
          input a from "../outside.txt"

  example check {"files": {"sub/data/t.txt": "hello,\r\nworld"}}

  example check {"files": {"t.txt": "t", "b.txt": "\ufeffbom"}}
    input files."s.duramen"

  example check {"files": {"t.txt": "t\n"}}

req SY-012 "Tables"
  decision D-011, D-015, D-016, D-017, D-018, D-022, D-023
  text
    `table <op>` writes examples of one operation as rows: the lines under it that start with
    `|`, indented four spaces or more (a row indented three MUST get P006). Any other line
    under it that is neither blank nor a comment MUST get P006 too. A row's cells are the texts
    between its `|` characters, where `\|` is a `|` inside a cell, the `|` at the end of the
    row may be left out, and the white space around a cell is not part of it. A row of only
    `|`, `-`, `:` and white space, which starts and ends with `|`, is a separator and is skipped
    wherever it is. The first other row is the header. A table without an op, with an op of more than
    one word, or with fewer than a header and one row MUST get P013, and then nothing else in
    the table is checked, except that a line under it that is no row, and neither blank nor a
    comment, still gets P006.

    A header names each column once, else P013. A header cell is a name, which runs to the
    first white space, `±` or `+-`, optionally followed by `±` (or `+-`) and a tolerance,
    which is the rest of the cell; anything else after the name makes the cell of no form. A
    name is an expectation path when it is `result`, `audit`, `error` or `id`, alone or
    followed by `.` and the rest of the path (whose names may be empty, REQ-OR-003, and may
    hold `=`, `≈` and `~`, which end a path only in an `expect` line), even when the operation
    declares an input field of that name; any other name of ASCII letters, digits, `_` and `-`
    is the name of an input field. A tolerance is a JSON number of 0 or more, else P010; a
    tolerance after an input field MUST get P010 too; and a column whose tolerance gets P010
    has none. The header's cells are read from the left: the first cell
    of any other form, or that names a column again, MUST get P013, and then nothing else in
    the table is checked, though a tolerance problem in a cell before it is still reported.
    Every other row is an example: one with a
    different number of cells from the header MUST get P014. An empty cell states nothing. A
    cell under an input field is that field's value, and a cell under an expectation path an
    expectation of that value (within the column's tolerance, if it has one), or of the
    oracle's value when the cell is `?`. Every other cell in a column with a tolerance is a
    JSON number, else P010, and in any other column, JSON, else P009.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node echo.mjs
      op f
        input x? json, y? json
      req A "a"
        table f
          | x        | y | result.x | result.y ± 0.5 |
          |----------|---|:--------:|----------------|
          | "a\|b"   |   | "a\|b"   |                |
          | 1        | 2 | ?        | 2.4            |
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      req A "a"
        table f
        table f g
          | x |
          | 1 |
        table f
          | x |
        table f
          | x | result ± -1 |
          | 1 | 2           |
        table f
          | x | result ± 0.5 |
          | 1 | "2"          |
        table f
          | x | y |
          | 1 |
          | {  | 2 |
          x | 1
        table f
          | x | |
          | 1 | 2 |
        table f
          | x ± 1 |
          | 1     |
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P013", "s.duramen:5: error P013", "s.duramen:8: error P013", "s.duramen:11: error P010", "s.duramen:15: error P010", "s.duramen:18: error P014", "s.duramen:19: error P009", "s.duramen:20: error P006", "s.duramen:22: error P013", "s.duramen:25: error P010"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      req A "a"
        table f g
          | x |
          | {bad |
        table f
         | x |
          | 1 |
        table f
          | a.b | result |
          | 1   | 2      |
        table f
          | x | result ± lots |
          | 1 | "two"         |
        table f
          | x | result ± 1 2 | result.y+-0.5 |
          | 1 | 2            | 3             |
        table f
          | x | x |
          | 1 | 2 |
        table f
          | x | result ± 0.5 |
          | 1 | 2.25 [       |
          | { | ?            |
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P013", "s.duramen:7: error P013", "s.duramen:8: error P006", "s.duramen:11: error P013", "s.duramen:14: error P010", "s.duramen:17: error P010", "s.duramen:20: error P013", "s.duramen:24: error P010", "s.duramen:25: error P009"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node echo.mjs
      op f
        input x? json
      req A "a"
        table f
          |---|----------|
          | x | result.x |
          |   |
          | 1 | 1
          |
          | 2 | 2        |
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      op f
        input a int
      req A "a"
        text
          T.
        table f
          | a ± 1 | b! | result ± x |
          | 1 | 2 | 3 |
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:9: error P010", "s.duramen:9: error P013"]
  example check {"files": {"s.duramen": "duramen 0.1\nspec s 1\noracle node echo.mjs\nop f\n  input answer? json, id? json\nreq A \"a\"\n  table f\n    | answer | result.k=1 | result.k~2 ± 0.5 | id |\n    |\u00a0---\t|---|:-:|\u3000|\n    | {\"result\": {\"k=1\": 1, \"k~2\": 2.25}} | 1 | 2 | \"A#1\" |\n  table f\n    | answer | result.a b |\n    | 1 | 2 |\n"}}

  example check {}

          | 1 |
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:9: error T002"]
  example check {}

        table f g
          not a row
          | x |
          | 1 |
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P013", "s.duramen:5: error P006"]

req SY-013 "Numbers too large for binary64"
  decision D-017
  text
    JSON in a record (an example's input, request members, an expectation's value, a table's
    cells) holds its numbers as IEEE 754 binary64 values, the values REQ-OR-003 compares. A
    number too large to be finite as one, such as `1e400`, cannot be written back into a
    request line or a suite (REQ-SU-003, REQ-SU-004), so JSON that holds one MUST get P009,
    and such a number MUST get P010 where REQ-SY-010 and REQ-SY-012 want a number, and P018
    in a `tolerance` clause. JSON that holds one gets P009 and nothing else for that text: not
    P012 when it is not an object, and not P051 when it sets `id`. A raw example is sent as it
    is written, so it can send one.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
        request {"x": 1e400}
      op f
        input a int
      req A "a"
        text
          T.
        example f {"a": 1e400}
        example f {"a": 1}
          expect result.a = [1, -1e400]
          request {"y": 1e999}
        table f
          | a | result |
          | 1e999 | 1 |
        example raw '{"id":"r","op":"f","input":{"a":1e400}}'
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error P009", "s.duramen:9: error P009", "s.duramen:11: error P009", "s.duramen:12: error P009", "s.duramen:15: error P009"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      op f
        input a int
        tolerance result.x 1e400
      req A "a"
        text
          T.
        example f {"a": 1}
          expect result ≈ 1e400 ± 1
          expect result ≈ 1 ± 1e400
        table f
          | a | result ± 1e400 |
          | 1 | 2 |
        table f
          | a | result ± 1 |
          | 1 | 1e400 |
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:5: error P018", "s.duramen:10: error P010", "s.duramen:11: error P010", "s.duramen:13: error P010", "s.duramen:17: error P010"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      op f
        request {"id": 1e400}
      req A "a"
        text
          T.
        example f [1e400]
        example f 1e400
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P009", "s.duramen:8: error P009", "s.duramen:9: error P009"]

section CK "Checking a record"
  text
    These checks run on a record that was read without errors (REQ-RC-005). Most example
    records here have an oracle, the small program shown under Files (`fixtures/echo.mjs`),
    which answers each request with its input as the result, so that their examples run
    cleanly and the diagnostics shown are the ones each example is about.

req CK-001 "Every requirement has an example"
  text
    A requirement with no example and no table row MUST get T001 at its line. (In the rest of
    the language, a static check, a property or evidence can stand in for an example.)
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      req A "a"
        text
          It MUST work.
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error T001"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      req A "a"
        table f
          | x |
          |---|
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error P013"]

req CK-002 "IDs are unique"
  decision D-013, D-018
  text
    The IDs of requirements MUST be unique among requirements, and so MUST those of open items
    among open items, those of decisions among decisions, and the names of operations among
    operations: every use after the first, in record order, MUST get T007 at its line, and an
    example is checked against the first operation of its name. IDs of different kinds may be
    the same: a requirement and an open item are REQ-x and OPEN-x, and a decision named
    `REQ-A` is no requirement.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node echo.mjs
      op f
        input x? json
      req A "a"
        example f {}
      req A "again"
        example f {}
      open A "an open item may share a requirement's ID"
        text
          Open.
      open B "b"
        text
          Open.
      open B "b again"
        text
          Open.
      decision D-1 "d"
        source s
      decision D-1 "d again"
        source s
      req C "c"
        decision D-1
        example f {}
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:8: error T007", "s.duramen:16: error T007", "s.duramen:21: error T007"]
  example check {}
    input files."a.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node echo.mjs
      op f
        input x? json
      req A "a"
        example f {}
    input files."b.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      req A "a"
        example f {}
      op f
        input y? json
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["b.duramen:2: error T007", "b.duramen:4: error T007"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node echo.mjs
      op f
        input x? json
      req A "a"
        decision REQ-A, OPEN-B
        example f {}
      decision REQ-A "named like a requirement"
        source s
      decision OPEN-B "named like an open item"
        source s
      open B "b"
        text
          Open.
      req A "a third time"
        example f {}
      req A "and a third"
        example f {}
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:16: error T007", "s.duramen:18: error T007"]

req CK-003 "Cited decisions are declared"
  decision D-015
  text
    Every decision a requirement cites MUST be declared; each one that is not MUST get T008 at
    the requirement's line, once however many times the requirement cites it.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node echo.mjs
      op f
        input x? json
      decision D-1 "d"
        source s

        decision D-2
        example f {}
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:8: error T008", "s.duramen:8: error T008"]

req CK-004 "Examples of declared operations"
  decision D-011
  text
    An example that expects no error and is not raw MUST name a declared operation, else T009
    at its line. Its input MUST have every field the operation declares without `?`, else T010
    for each one missing, and each field of its input that the operation does not declare MUST
    get the warning T011. For a table row, the line is the row's. An example that expects an
    error (an expectation whose path is `error` itself), or is raw, is not checked against the
    operation: it may be about a request the operation would refuse.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node echo.mjs
      op f
        input a number, b? number
      errors
        e when never
      req A "a"
        example g {"a": 1}
        example f {"b": 1}
        example f {"a": 1, "c": 2}
        example f
        example g {"answer": {"error": "e"}}
          expect error = "e"
        example raw '{"id": "A#6", "op": "g"}'

          | b | c |

req CK-005 "Expected errors are declared"
  decision D-011, D-018
  text
    Every value an example states for the path `error` MUST be a code declared under `errors`:
    in `expect error = <value>`, in `expect error ≈ <number> ± <tolerance>`, and in a cell of
    an `error` column, with a tolerance or without; else T023 at the expectation's line, for a
    table row at the row's. A value that is not a string is never a declared code.
    `expect error = ?` and a `?` cell name no code.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node echo.mjs
      op f
        input answer? json
      errors
        e when never
      req A "a"
        example f {"answer": {"error": "e"}}
          expect error = "e"
        example f {"answer": {"error": "nope"}}
          expect error = "nope"
        example raw '{"id": "r", "op": "f", "input": {"answer": {"error": "other"}}}'
          expect error = "other"
        example f {"answer": {"error": "e"}}
          expect error = ?
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:12: error T023", "s.duramen:14: error T023"]
  example check {}

        table f

          | {"error": 2}     | 2         |
          | {"error": "e"}   | ?         |
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:10: error T023", "s.duramen:13: error T023"]

req CK-006 "Obligations live in requirements"
  decision D-006, D-014, D-021, D-022
  text
    The words MUST, MUST NOT, SHALL, SHALL NOT and REQUIRED, in capitals and as whole words,
    state obligations, and obligations belong in requirements, where they have an ID and
    examples. Outside requirements, a text holding such a word MUST get one T004: the text of
    the spec, of a section, of a note or of a decision (at that statement's line), each
    rejected alternative of a decision (at the decision's line), an operation's `result` (at
    the `op` line), and each condition under `errors` (at its clause's line). The text of an
    open item holding such a word MUST get the warning T014 at the open item's line. A word is
    whole when no ASCII letter, ASCII digit or `_` touches it, so `MUST-have` and `MUSTé` hold
    MUST. A word inside a quotation on one line, between `"` and `"`, `“` and `”`, or a pair
    of backquotes, is not such a word (the lines of a condition, and of a rejected alternative
    once its JSON string is read, are lines here too, ended at LF, CR LF or a lone CR as in
    REQ-SY-001), and titles are not checked;
    ``` ``MUST`` ``` is MUST between two empty quotations. A quotation is not part of the words
    around it: ``` x`a`MUST ``` holds MUST, and ``` MU`a`ST ``` holds no word.
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
        text
          The program MUST work.
      op f
        result what it MUST return
      errors
        e when it SHALL fail
      section S "It MUST be titled"
        text
          REQUIRED reading.
      note
        text
          This note says `MUST`, "SHALL" and “REQUIRED”, MUSTARD and must.
      decision D-1 "d"
        source s
        text
          Fine.
        rejected "Another MUST."
      open O "o"
        text
          It MUST NOT be.
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:2: error T004", "s.duramen:5: error T004", "s.duramen:8: error T004", "s.duramen:9: error T004", "s.duramen:15: error T004", "s.duramen:15: warning T012", "s.duramen:20: warning T014"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      decision D-1 "d"
        source s
        text
          It MUST.
        rejected "It SHALL."
        rejected "It is REQUIRED."
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error T004", "s.duramen:3: error T004", "s.duramen:3: error T004", "s.duramen:3: warning T012"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      errors
        e when the "MUST
          hold" rule fails
        f when the "MUST hold" rule fails
      note
        text
          A MUST-have.
      section S "s"
        text
          MUSTé
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:4: error T004", "s.duramen:7: error T004", "s.duramen:10: error T004"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      section T "t"
        text
          It ``MUST`` be, and it `MUST` not.
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error T004"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1

      note
        text
          x`a`MUST
      note
        text
          MU`a`ST, and "MU"ST
      note
        text
          A"q"SHALL

  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1

        source s
        text
          Fine.
        rejected "\"It\rMUST\" be"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:3: error T004", "s.duramen:3: warning T012"]

req CK-007 "Open items are not tested"

  text
    An open item is deliberately left unspecified, so each `example` or `table` clause of an

  example check {}

req CK-008 "The order of errors is stated once"
  decision D-007, D-011
  text
    The order in which errors are checked is stated once, by the order of the `errors` list. A
    requirement's text that names two or more of the codes declared there, each as a whole word
    (not next to an ASCII letter, ASCII digit, `_` or `-`), and holds one of the phrases "in
    this order", "in the order", "first that applies", "first match", "precede", "precedes",
    "preceded", "before", "after", "take precedence" and "takes precedence" (as whole words:
    not next to an ASCII letter, ASCII digit or `_`; in any letter case; with any white space
    between the words of a phrase, a line break included), MUST get T005 at its `text`
    clause's line. A letter outside ASCII touches neither: `too_bigé` names `too_big`, and
    `before-hand` holds "before".
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node echo.mjs
      op f
        input x? json
      errors
        too_big when x > 9
        too_small when x < 0
      req A "a"
        text
          A request that is too_big gets too_big, and one too_small gets too_small.
        example f {}
      req B "b"
        text
          too_big is checked Before too_small.
        example f {}
      req C "c"
        text
          too_big is checked first.
          After that, nothing.
        example f {}
      req D "d"
        text
          too_big and too_small are checked in this
          order.
        example f {}
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = ["s.duramen:14: error T005", "s.duramen:23: error T005"]
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node echo.mjs
      op f
        input x? json
      errors
        e when x
        f when y
      req A "a"
        text
          A request may be refused before it is read: see the errors list.
        example f {}
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
    expect result.diagnostics = []
  example check {}
    input files."s.duramen"
      duramen 0.1
      spec s 1
      oracle node echo.mjs
      op f
        input x? json
      errors
        too_big when x > 9
        too_small when x < 0
      req A "a"
        text
          too_bigé, then too_small: decided before-hand.
        example f {}
      req B "b"
        text
          xtoo_big and too_small2 come after.
        example f {}
    input files."echo.mjs" from "fixtures/echo.mjs"
